findings.title: WebSocket framing contract is incorrect for .NET receivers
findings.evidence: "WebSocket frame boundaries define message boundaries" and "Large messages that fragment at the WebSocket layer are reassembled by System.Net.WebSockets before deserialization."
findings.problem: The spec conflates WebSocket frames with messages and assumes .NET delivers a fully reassembled message automatically. In System.Net.WebSockets, receivers must read until EndOfMessage before deserializing.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers following this text will deserialize partial payloads or enforce limits on fragments instead of complete messages, causing immediate interop failures on fragmented messages.
findings.proposed_fix: State that one JSON document maps to one WebSocket message, require receivers to accumulate frames until EndOfMessage=true, and define that the 4 MiB limit applies to the reassembled message size.

findings.title: Oversize-message streaming is undefined
findings.evidence: "Maximum single-message size: 4 MiB. Above this, the sender breaks the payload ... into streamed smaller messages."
findings.problem: The spec requires chunking above 4 MiB but defines no chunk message types, correlation fields, sequence numbers, completion marker, retry behavior, or reassembly rules.
findings.why_it_matters: Any payload that exceeds 4 MiB cannot be implemented interoperably or tested, especially feature-tree transfers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit chunked-message wire types and reassembly/error semantics, or remove streaming from v1 and require pagination/compression through separately defined result types.

findings.title: Stretch tools are included in the protocol before their wire shapes exist
findings.evidence: "This spec defines every type that crosses a process boundary" and "Full field definitions are deferred to stretch implementation ... // TODO: STRETCH markers so the polymorphic registrations are complete from day one."
findings.problem: The document claims to fully define the wire contract, but stretch-tool inputs/results are intentionally left undefined while still being planned for registration.
findings.why_it_matters: Schemas, validators, serializers, and registry completeness tests cannot be implemented without actual fields, and later filling them in changes the protocol contract retroactively.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove stretch tools from protocol registration until they are fully specified, or define complete input/result records now.

findings.title: Tool naming has two unsynchronized sources of truth
findings.location: Section 2.4 "Polymorphic Discriminators"; Section 4.3 "IToolInput and IToolResult"; Section 11 "Tool Registry and Schema Generation"
findings.evidence: "IToolInput and IToolResult: discriminator property \"tool\" with value equal to the tool name" and "ToolRegistry.All reflects the Protocol assembly ... finding every type with [ToolName] attributes"
findings.problem: The wire discriminator uses one naming mechanism and the registry/schema system uses another, but the spec does not define a single authoritative source or a test that they match.
findings.why_it_matters: A mismatch creates tools that serialize under one name and register/schema-generate under another, causing runtime lookup failures and integration churn.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one authoritative tool name source and add a build-breaking test that discriminator value, ToolNameAttribute, timeout entry, and schema name are identical.

findings.title: StateSnapshot cannot represent transient sketch selections
findings.evidence: "SketchEntityId" is "Transient, valid only within the active sketch session" while `StateSnapshot.ActiveSelection` is `IReadOnlyList<EntityRef>`.
findings.problem: During an active sketch, selected sketch entities are transient and modeled by SketchEntityId, but the snapshot only allows persistent EntityRef values.
findings.why_it_matters: Selection-driven workflows in active sketches cannot be transmitted faithfully, forcing lossy conversion or hidden out-of-band state.
findings.proposed_fix: Change ActiveSelection to a discriminated union that can carry both persistent EntityRef and transient SketchEntityId values, and register/test that union.

findings.title: GetFeatureTreeInput.Compressed has no defined wire effect
findings.evidence: `public bool Compressed { get; init; } = true;` in `GetFeatureTreeInput`, but `GetFeatureTreeResult` only contains `IReadOnlyList<FeatureNode> Tree` and `string TreeHash`.
findings.problem: The request exposes a compression flag, but the response shape has no compressed payload field, algorithm indicator, or alternate encoding.
findings.why_it_matters: Callers cannot know what behavior to expect, and implementers will either ignore the flag or invent incompatible behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove Compressed from v1 or define an explicit compressed response contract with encoding algorithm and content fields.

findings.title: Closed wire vocabularies are modeled as unconstrained strings
findings.evidence: `Reason { get; init; } // "user_abort" | "timeout" | "agent_abort"`, `ErrorCode { get; init; } // "VERSION_MISMATCH" | ...`, while Section 14 only defines validators for `IToolInput`.
findings.problem: Several message fields have finite allowed tokens only in comments, but the actual contract type is string and there is no envelope validation/schema for them.
findings.why_it_matters: Typos and casing drift will not be caught by the type system or schema tests, breaking inter-process compatibility.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace these fields with enums/strong types or add explicit message-envelope validators and schema constraints for each allowed token set.

findings.title: Feature-tree hash determinism depends on unspecified array ordering
findings.evidence: `FeatureTree` and `Parameters` are lists, while hash rules only specify "sorted object keys" and say nothing about array ordering.
findings.problem: Canonicalization normalizes object key order but not list order. Equivalent trees emitted in different sibling/parameter orders will hash differently.
findings.why_it_matters: State change detection and any downstream hash-chain logic become unstable across implementations or traversal changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Define canonical ordering for every hashed list or explicitly reject non-canonical ordering before hashing, and add tests covering reordered-but-equivalent inputs.

top_3_must_fix: Define the complete wire contract for fragmented and >4 MiB messages, including receiver behavior and chunking/reassembly semantics.
Remove stretch tools from the registered protocol or fully specify every stretch-tool input/result record now.
Establish one authoritative tool name source and enforce equality across discriminators, registry entries, schema generation, and timeout lookup.
